title: Postgres in production — Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
context: P0-01 of the roadmap. ADR-0018 made the schema and migrations dialect-portable and proved them in CI against Postgres 16, but prod still ran on a single SQLite file on the Azure VM. That file is a one-disk-failure-away-from-total-data-loss surface, won't clear a bank security review, and blocks Phase-2 multi-tenancy (RLS requires Postgres). This ADR records the operational decision to cut production over, and the shape it takes.
decision: Production runs on Azure Database for PostgreSQL — Flexible Server, version 16, in the same region as the application VM. The application reaches it via TREASURY_DATABASE_URL, sourced from Azure Key Vault at boot (P0-06). SQLite stays as the default for local dev and the hermetic pytest suite (ADR-0018 invariant unchanged).
scope_in: Managed Postgres: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server 16, same region as the app VM, SSL enforced (sslmode=require), private endpoint or VM-only firewall allow-list — never public.
Backups: PITR enabled, 7-day retention minimum, geo-redundant where the region supports it. A restore drill is run before go-live and documented in scripts/.

Pool config in backend/app/db.py: pool_size=10, max_overflow=10, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800. SQLite path is unchanged. pool_pre_ping is load-bearing — Azure PG reaps idle connections and without it the first request after idle 500s.
Dedicated non-superuser role 'treasury_app' owns the 'treasury' database. The application never connects as a superuser.
Connection string lives in Key Vault, not in a VM env file. Interim env-var deployment is acceptable but tracked as debt against P0-06.
scope_out_deferred: Read replicas. Single primary is fine until the load shape is known.
PgBouncer / external pooler. Flexible Server's built-in pooler is enough at this size.
Per-tenant database routing (data residency). That lands with the multi-tenancy plan — see PHASE_2_MULTITENANCY_PLAN.md §6.
Running the full pytest suite against Postgres — still deferred (ADR-0018). The CI migration-and-seed job plus the production footprint is the coverage.
Removing SQLite as a supported dialect. Dev + tests keep it.
invariants: Production TREASURY_DATABASE_URL always points at Postgres. SQLite in prod is a regression, not a configuration choice.
The DB role used by the app is never a superuser and never has BYPASSRLS (reserved for the platform-admin role when the multi-tenancy plan unparks).
pool_pre_ping stays true. Removing it to shave latency has already been tried mentally and rejected — the failure mode is a user-visible 500 after lunch.
Backups are only backups once a restore has been performed into a scratch database and a row read out. Untested backups do not count.
consequences: backend/app/db.py — pool config added behind the SQLite/Postgres branch.
Operational: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server provisioned, PITR enabled, restore drill documented in scripts/.
Secrets: TREASURY_DATABASE_URL moves to Key Vault (ties to P0-06).
Unblocks PHASE_2_MULTITENANCY_PLAN.md Stage 1 — RLS requires a real Postgres bind in the target deployment.
P3-03 (backup + snapshot) is subsumed by the PITR + restore-drill clauses of this ADR.
